title: Elderly husband downplays: wife 'a bit sleepy' (cardiac arrest)

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, good evening, I'm sorry to bother you, it's probably nothing.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: My wife, she's a bit sleepy, she sat down in the chair and now she's, she won't really answer me.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Kastanjegatan 3, Dalby. It's a yellow house.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Kastanjegatan 3, Dalby. Go to her now. Shake her shoulders and shout her name. Does she react?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Margit! Margit! ... No. No, she doesn't. Her eyes are half open.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Is she breathing? Look at her chest.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: She's breathing kind of funny, like snoring, every now and then. She does that sometimes when she sleeps.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Okay, listen to me carefully. That is not normal breathing. I'm sending an ambulance now with sirens. We're going to start CPR together.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: CPR? Oh God. Is she, is she...

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Can you get her down on the floor, on her back?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I'll try, she's heavy. Okay. Okay she's on the floor.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Put the heel of your hand in the middle of her chest, the other hand on top. Push down hard and fast. Count out loud with me. One, two, three, four...

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Good, keep going, don't stop. Is there anyone else in the house? Is there a defibrillator nearby?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: No, just us. I don't know about a defibrillator. Twenty-eight, twenty-nine...
